district.description: The capital city of Tamil Nadu, formerly known as Madras. It is a major cultural hub renowned for its colonial heritage, classical Carnatic music season, bustling beaches, and ancient neighborhood temples like Mylapore.

culturalEntries.title: Kapaleeshwarar Temple, Mylapore
culturalEntries.shortDescription: An iconic Dravidian-style temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, renowned for its towering gopuram and the grand annual Arupathumoovar festival.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Located in the historic neighborhood of Mylapore, the Kapaleeshwarar Temple is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture. Originally built around the 7th century CE by the Pallavas and later rebuilt by the Vijayanagara kings in the 16th century after the original was destroyed, it remains the cultural epicenter of Chennai. The temple is intricately linked to the Tamil Shaivite saints (Nayanmars) and hosts the spectacular Panguni Peruvizha, highlighted by the Arupathumoovar procession.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Original structure dates to the 7th century Pallava era; current structure rebuilt in the 16th century Vijayanagara style.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: A vibrant center for Tamil Hindu traditions, Carnatic music, and the annual Panguni festival which draws thousands of devotees to witness the chariot procession.
culturalEntries.festivalsCustoms: Panguni Peruvizha with the 63 Nayanmars (Arupathumoovar) procession; Maha Shivaratri, Navaratri
culturalEntries.relatedArts: Carnatic music concerts, Bharatanatyam, Tevaram hymns
culturalEntries.traditionalClothing: Silk sarees for women, traditional veshti and angavastram for men
culturalEntries.traditionalCuisine: Mylapore filter coffee, traditional temple prasadam, medu vada, pongal
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: Tevaram Hymns; Tamil Nadu HR&CE Department records; Archaeological Survey of India

culturalEntries.title: San Thome Basilica
culturalEntries.alternateNames: St. Thomas Cathedral Basilica, San Thome Church
culturalEntries.shortDescription: Neo-Gothic Roman Catholic minor basilica built over the reputed tomb of St. Thomas the Apostle.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Constructed in 1893 by the British over earlier 16th-century Portuguese church foundations, San Thome Basilica is one of only three known basilicas in the world built directly over the tomb of an apostle of Jesus Christ. Built in striking Neo-Gothic style with towering white spires, stained-glass windows depicting the life of Christ, and a subterranean tomb chapel and museum, it is a foremost pilgrimage center for Christians across India.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Built in 1893 on the site of earlier 16th-century Portuguese churches; tradition holds that St. Thomas reached the Coromandel Coast in 52 CE.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: A landmark of Chennai's multi-faith coastal heritage and an internationally revered pilgrimage center.
culturalEntries.festivalsCustoms: Feast of St. Thomas (July 3), Christmas Midnight Mass, Easter celebrations
culturalEntries.relatedArts: Sacred choral music, Christian hymnology, ecclesiastical architecture
culturalEntries.traditionalClothing: Sunday choir vestments, traditional festival attire
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: Archdiocese of Madras-Mylapore records; Archaeological Survey of India

culturalEntries.title: Fort St. George & St. Mary's Church
culturalEntries.titleTa: புனித ஜார்ஜ் கோட்டை மற்றும் புனித மேரி தேவாலயம்
culturalEntries.alternateNames: Fort St. George, Seat of Tamil Nadu Government
culturalEntries.shortDescription: The first English fortress in India, founded in 1640, now housing the Tamil Nadu Secretariat and Archaeological Museum.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Erected by the British East India Company in 1639-40, Fort St. George formed the nucleus around which the modern metropolis of Madras grew. Inside its granite ramparts stands St. Mary's Church (the oldest Anglican church east of Suez, consecrated in 1680), Clive House, and the Fort Museum displaying colonial weaponry, coins, uniforms, and original letters. Today, it serves as the official administrative seat of the Government of Tamil Nadu.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Constructed by Francis Day and Andrew Cogan of the British East India Company beginning in 1639.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: The birthplace of modern urban Chennai and the epicenter of Tamil Nadu's democratic governance.
culturalEntries.festivalsCustoms: Independence Day and Republic Day ceremonial flag-hoisting
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: Archaeological Survey of India Fort Museum; Government of Tamil Nadu Archives

culturalEntries.title: Chennai Margazhi Carnatic Music Season
culturalEntries.shortDescription: One of the world's largest cultural music festivals, featuring hundreds of Carnatic concerts across historic Chennai Sabhas.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Originating in 1927 to commemorate the founding of the Madras Music Academy, the Margazhi Music Season spans mid-December to mid-January. Over a thousand Carnatic vocalists, veena, violin, and mridangam artists, and Bharatanatyam exponents perform across prestigious cultural institutions (Sabhas) such as the Music Academy, Narada Gana Sabha, and Krishna Gana Sabha, accompanied by traditional Sabha canteen delicacies.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Inaugurated in December 1927 alongside the All India Congress Session, evolving into an annual tradition.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: Celebrated globally as one of the world's largest classical music festivals, preserving centuries-old Carnatic ragas and compositions of the Trimurti.
culturalEntries.festivalsCustoms: Margazhi morning bhajans, daily sabha concerts, lecture-demonstrations
culturalEntries.relatedArts: Carnatic vocal, Veena, Mridangam, Ghatam, Bharatanatyam
culturalEntries.traditionalClothing: Silk sarees with temple borders, traditional veshti and angavastram
culturalEntries.traditionalCuisine: Sabha canteen delicacies: Asoka halwa, Keerai vadai, Elaneer payasam, Madras filter coffee
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: The Music Academy Madras historical archives; Tamil Nadu Tourism
